verifications.claim_text: ChatGPT's lower frequency of stance features leaves it unable to offer accurate rhetorical and pragmatic feedback.
verifications.evidence_quote: This more retiring or ‘invisible’ stance means that ChatGPT is unable to accurately offer feedback on rhetorical and pragmatic aspects of arguments produced by real human writers.
verifications.explanation: The claim's central proposition — that ChatGPT's lower frequency of stance features leaves it unable to offer accurate rhetorical and pragmatic feedback — is stated in the source almost verbatim: "This more retiring or 'invisible' stance means that ChatGPT is unable to accurately offer feedback on rhetorical and pragmatic aspects of arguments produced by real human writers." The peripheral proposition that ChatGPT uses stance features at a lower frequency is also supported by Table 3 and the accompanying text: "we found that the ChatGPT 4 essays, though structurally coherent and logically organised, contained a significantly lower frequency of features such as hedges, boosters, attitude markers, and self-mention (Table 3)." No assertion is contradicted and no hedge is removed, so the claim is verified.

verifications.evidence_quote: ChatGPT remained consistently high in precision regardless of prompts, being 94%, 98% and 94% respectively for GPT-P1, GPT-P2 and GPT-P3, higher than Grammarly (85%).
verifications.explanation: All propositions are supported. The precision figures (94%, 98%, 94%) match the source verbatim: "ChatGPT remained consistently high in precision regardless of prompts, being 94%, 98% and 94% respectively for GPT-P1, GPT-P2 and GPT-P3" and the Total row of Table 1 (94, 98, 94). The recall figures (10%, 33%, 55%) match: "the recall of ChatGPT considerably improved across prompts, with that of GPT-P1, GPT-P2 and GPT-P3 being 10%, 33% and 55% respectively" and Table 1's Total row (10, 33, 55). The four high-frequency categories overtaken are stated: "it far outstripped Grammarly in correctly spotting the four categories accounting for most of the errors in the corpus (62%, 206/334), namely errors of direct translation ... word choice or expression ... sentence structure ... and pronoun". The five categories lagged are stated: "ChatGPT across prompts lagged behind Grammarly in five error categories (1/3 of all categories), namely errors of article/determiner ... preposition ... spelling ... verb form ... and word form". No assertion is contradicted, absent, or hedged.

evidence_quotes: ChatGPT remained consistently high in precision regardless of prompts, being 94%, 98% and 94% respectively for GPT-P1, GPT-P2 and GPT-P3, higher than Grammarly (85%).
In contrast, the recall of ChatGPT considerably improved across prompts, with that of GPT-P1, GPT-P2 and GPT-P3 being 10%, 33% and 55% respectively.

Conspicuously, it far outstripped Grammarly in correctly spotting the four categories accounting for most of the errors in the corpus (62%, 206/334), namely errors of direct translation (37/54, 69% for GPT-P3 vs. 1/54, 2% for Grammarly), word choice or expression (37/76, 49% for GPT-P3 vs. 16/76, 21% for Grammarly), sentence structure (23/39, 59% for GPT-P3 vs. 13/39, 33% for Grammarly) and pronoun (15/36, 42% for GPT-P3 vs. 7/36, 19% for Grammarly).

Admittedly, ChatGPT across prompts lagged behind Grammarly in five error categories (1/3 of all categories), namely errors of article/determiner (5/20, 25% for GPT-P3 vs. 11/20, 55% for Grammarly), preposition (4/7, 57% for GPT-P3 vs. 7/7, 100% for Grammarly), spelling (14/15, 93% for GPT-P3 vs. 15/15, 100% for Grammarly), verb form (11/16, 69% for GPT-P3 vs. 14/16, 88% for Grammarly) and word form (2/6, 33% for GPT-P3 vs. 3/6, 50% for Grammarly).
